rules.quote: For GPT-5.6 and later: "In the Responses API, set `prompt_cache_options.ttl` to choose the minimum cache lifetime", with values "30m" (default) and "12h". "These are total write rates, not surcharges on top of ordinary input": 1.25x input for 30m and 2.5x input for 12h. The pricing page lists gpt-6.1-sol writes at $2.50/$5.00, long context $5/$10, and gpt-6-luna at $0.125/$0.25.

Earlier models: "Use `prompt_cache_retention`, with supported values that depend on the model". Values are `in_memory` and `24h`. The named extended-retention models are gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.2, gpt-5.1-codex-max, gpt-5.1, gpt-5.1-codex, gpt-5.1-codex-mini, gpt-5.1-chat-latest, gpt-5, gpt-5-codex and gpt-4.1. Earlier models have "No additional cache-write charge". Only the listed rows present in the seed are curated here; no TTL write prices are claimed for them.
"GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5 Pro support `24h` only". Earlier models have "No additional cache-write charge". These retention-only rows have no TTL write-price claim.

Caching is supported on "all active Claude models". "Cache write tokens with a 5-minute TTL are 1.25 times the base input tokens price." "Cache write tokens with a 1-hour TTL are 2 times the base input tokens price." The Messages API types set the default ttl to 5m. The pricing page lists claude-opus-5-5 input at $4, 5m writes at $5, and 1h writes at $8.
